Title: Re_gent: Version Control for AI agent Activity | Product Hunt
## Version Control for AI agent Activity. Git for your AI agent’s actions. re\_gent shows what your coding agent changed, which prompt caused it, and lets you roll back agent work across files and sessions. ### If you followed re\_gent, you’ll probably like this too. A lot of you followed re\_gent because you felt the same pain we did:. AI agents are writing more code, but understanding what they did, why they did it, and what broke afterwards is still way too messy. No reviews yetBe the first to leave a review for Re\_gent. Linking agent file changes to the exact prompt that triggered them is genuinely novel. How do you handle rollback when the agent touched external state or APIs? Is it purely file-level undo or does re\_gent track side effects too? At the moment we are tracking only context and file states. We do want to try to track side effects but it requires a much more robust understanding of the change (perhaps through external llm / some sort of semantic understanding). If you have any ideas we would we'd love to hear them! At RetainSure we've felt the pain of debugging a bad agent decision without any state history to trace it back through. At the moment most of the coding agents have this capability out of the box (/branch for Claude Code). The rgt blame feature is what caught my attention — tracing a line of code back to the exact prompt that caused it is genuinely useful for debugging. Curious if it works with Claude Code already or if that's still on the roadmap? Re\_gent feels like that same observability idea but applied at the file/code level, which is actually where it hurts more. The prompt-to-diff linking is the feature I'd use most.. I run 15+ automated agents in production and the worst debugging scenario is "something changed overnight and I don't know which agent did it." Right now my workaround is JSON audit trails per agent, but tracing a bad outcome back to the specific prompt that caused it is still manual detective work.

This is the kind of tool where you don't know you needed it until you've been using it for a week and then can't go back. I run Claude Code and Pipali simultaneously pretty often, and the main friction before this was context switching just to check if something had finished. The notch indicator is clean and stays out of the way. The thing I'd love next could be a way to distinguish which agent is active when multiple are running at once, even just by color or icon. Right now it's a single ambient signal is useful, but when things go quiet it's not obvious if the task finished, errored out, or is just waiting on a long API call. Title: Re_gent | Version Control for AI agent Activity | Product Hunt
# Re\_gent. ## Version Control for AI agent Activity. ### Trending products. Linking agent file changes to the exact prompt that triggered them is genuinely novel. Most agent frameworks hand you a diff with no causal chain. How do you handle rollback when the agent touched external state or APIs? Is it purely file-level undo or does re\_gent track side effects too? At the moment we are tracking only context and file states. We do want to try to track side effects but it requires a much more robust understanding of the change (perhaps through external llm / some sort of semantic understanding). If you have any ideas we would we'd love to hear them! Treating agent activity as a versioned artifact you can diff and revert is genuinely clever. At RetainSure we've felt the pain of debugging a bad agent decision without any state history to trace it back through. Does Re\_gent support mid-run checkpointing so you can fork from a specific state, or is versioning scoped to full run boundaries? At the moment most of the coding agents have this capability out of the box (/branch for Claude Code). We have a detailed roadmap (with the fork functionality). Lots of new capabilities in re\_gent's roadmap. The rgt blame feature is what caught my attention — tracing a line of code back to the exact prompt that caused it is genuinely useful for debugging. Curious if it works with Claude Code already or if that's still on the roadmap? Re\_gent feels like that same observability idea but applied at the file/code level, which is actually where it hurts more. The prompt-to-diff linking is the feature I'd use most.. if an agent takes two different approaches across sessions on the same file, does re\_gent track those as separate branches or does it flatten everything into one linear history? I run 15+ automated agents in production and the worst debugging scenario is "something changed overnight and I don't know which agent did it." Right now my workaround is JSON audit trails per agent, but tracing a bad outcome back to the specific prompt that caused it is still manual detective work.
